key_insight: Lateral inflow changes the stability of sudden expansion flow, creating a regime where symmetry breaking disappears and the jet no longer has a critical Reynolds threshold to deflect.
engineering_relevance: Designs involving confined expansions and side feeds can use the lateral-to-central flow ratio to control or suppress flow instabilities and jet偏偏 deflection.
method: Experiments in a symmetric 3D confined sudden expansion with lateral inflow
Linear stability analysis and weakly nonlinear theory
Direct numerical simulations to validate flow regimes
evidence_signal: Across Reynolds numbers below 300, the study identifies three regimes and shows that outside an intermediate lateral-flow band the bifurcation is supercritical, while inside that band DNS finds no intrinsic amplification.
watch_item: Experimentally observed fluctuations in the intermediate lateral-flow band are not explained by the models, and geometric imperfections may dominate the residual asymmetry.
paper_title: Sudden expansion stability thresholds modified by lateral flows
